- **AC-156** (auto) [LY-12 d] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN a door animated through every `area` value 0 → `area_max` → 0 one step per tick for 128 ticks (the formula's property under a stepped test driver; the MVP door itself is binary) WHEN `static_version` is read before and after THEN it was bumped **0 times**, `leaf_version` was bumped once per tick on which `leaf_w` changed, and a `StubEmitterVersionCache` that keys its static layer on `static_version` rebuilt that layer 0 times and patched its leaves once per change.
- **AC-55** (auto) [LY-11, D.5] GIVEN `door_cryo_s` at `area` 32 and a foot box `[296, 312) × [384, 392)` WHEN a PLAYER-origin close to `area` 20 is validated (`leaf_would_overlap` called with `opening_ref` = the door's opening `edge_id`, *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*) THEN `leaf_would_overlap` is true (leaf `[240, 306)`); the owner's token (`OBSTRUCTED`) is asserted in the owner's test, not here; `area` is unchanged and no dirty key is marked; GIVEN a SYSTEM-origin close THEN the owner enters `CLOSING_BLOCKED`, `area` holds at its last non-overlapping value, the command is re-processed at T+1 and the box's position is unchanged.
- **AC-56** (auto) [LY-11] GIVEN `boxes = [A, B]` where only B overlaps WHEN evaluated THEN `leaf_would_overlap` is true; `boxes = []` is false; two identical calls return identical answers; AND raising `area` from 0 to 64 with a box in the doorway never returns `OBSTRUCTED`.
- **AC-57** (auto) [LY-11] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: reframed as a formula property; the MVP door is binary, so there is no sweep)* GIVEN a test driver that steps `area` from 64 to 0 one unit per write with the foot box inside the doorway WHEN each write's NEW `area` is checked THEN the first write whose leaf overlaps the box is refused and `area` holds at its previous value, not at `CLOSED`; AND GIVEN the binary close (one jump to 0) with the same box THEN the single write is refused and `area` stays `area_max`.
- **AC-147** (auto) [LY-11, LY-15, D.5] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the mated-hatch case AC-55..57 did not test)* GIVEN the `fixture_airlock` weld (opening `area_max` 64, leaves A `[672, 696) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)` and B `[696, 720) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)`), `StubBodyFootBoxes` holding only the box `[696, 712) × [296, 304)` (overlaps B's leaf and not A's) WHEN `leaf_would_overlap(opening_ref = the hatch's edge_id, area = 20, boxes)` is evaluated for a close from `area` 32 THEN it is **true** (B's leaf `[696, 720) × [240, 306)` overlaps; a call evaluated against A's leaf alone would return false); AND with the box `[672, 688) × [296, 304)` (overlaps only A's leaf) THEN true; with `[696, 712) × [310, 318)` (below both leaves) THEN false; with the straddling box `[688, 704) × [296, 304)` THEN true and `leaf_obstruction` reports the first leaf in caller order; AND `leaf_would_overlap(unknown_edge, …)` returns false and raises `opening_unknown`.
- **AC-166** (auto) [LY-11, LY-16, LY-26 d] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN an interior door and a mated hatch WHEN `opening_leaves(edge_id)` is read THEN the interior door's opening yields exactly one `(section_id, slot)` and the hatch's yields exactly two, one per section, each at its own `section_offset`; AND after a save, restore and `post_restore` the map equals the pre-save map (it is derived from `welds[]` and `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`, never persisted).
- **AC-148** (manual, playtest; BLOCKED-ON the Interaction / art-director cue, OQ-31) [LY-11, Game Feel failure texture] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN a scripted session in which each of at least 5 first-time playtesters meets (a) a door held open by a crewmate standing in the doorway when they try to close it, and (b) a door with no power when they try to operate it WHEN each is asked, per door, "what is stopping this door?" and answers are coded by two reviewers THEN at least 4 of 5 attribute (a) to the body in the doorway and (b) to power, none attributes (a) to "the door is broken" or "no power", and the cue shown for (a) is never shown for (b) (the harness asserts `leaf_obstruction` returns `NONE` for the unpowered door because it never reaches the overlap test).
- **AC-58** (auto) [LY-9, LY-15, D.5] GIVEN the weld of `fixture_airlock` (hatch `area_max` 64) to `fixture_derelict_b_socket` (hatch `area_max` 128) with the doorway spanning body-frame `y` `[240, 336)` on both sides WHEN welded THEN one OPENING with `area_max = 64` exists; at `area` 0 both leaves cover `[240, 336)`; at `area` 32 both leaves are `[240, 288)` (the low-coordinate, north end; footprints `[672, 696)` and `[696, 720)`) and the gap is `[288, 336)`; at `area` 64 neither returns a rect; for an N- or S-facing mated pair both leaves anchor to the west end.
- **AC-59** (lint) [LY-9, LY-8 f, D.18] GIVEN one fixture per case WHEN linted THEN a hatch that declares a hinge raises `HATCH_HINGE_AUTHORED`; a door assembly at a corner `DOOR_AT_CORNER`; overlapping assemblies `DOOR_ASSEMBLY_OVERLAP`; a door within a socket frame `DOOR_NEAR_SOCKET`; a MACHINE footprint or wall-mounted prop in the pocket `DOOR_POCKET_CLEAR`; a door with no free 48 × 48 approach square `DOOR_APPROACH_CLEAR`; a `sill_room_key` that does not flank the door `DOOR_SILL_ROOM_INVALID`; a door with no `sill_room_key` `DOOR_SILL_UNOWNED`; `fixture_cryo_excerpt` passes (assembly `[144, 336)`, margin `384 − 336 = 48`); AND *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* a socket hatch on a 2-tile run whose LOW-side pocket would lie outside the run raises **none** of the `DOOR_POCKET_CLEAR` ids (hatches are exempt, LY-15 e), and a hatch whose `doorway_start_px` differs from its socket's `start_px` raises `HATCH_ALIGN` (both MVP fixtures pass: 240 = 240 and 144 = 144).
- **AC-60** (lint) [D.18] GIVEN two doors on one run WHEN the pitch is varied THEN hinge LOW + hinge LOW passes at 192 px and fails at 168; pockets pointing away pass at 96; pockets pointing toward each other pass at 288 and fail at 264; a non-hinge margin of 48 passes and 24 fails `DOOR_AT_CORNER`.
- **AC-61** (lint) [LY-9, LY-30] GIVEN `area_max` 0, 31 and 129 WHEN evaluated THEN `DOOR_AREA_MAX` rejects the template in BOOTING and D.5 is never evaluated (no division by zero reaches runtime); 32 and 128 pass; `width_px` 48 and 144 raise `DOOR_WIDTH`, 96 passes.
- **AC-62** (auto; opening-read double at unit level, real Graph read in the integration run — *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*) [LY-9 edge] GIVEN the stub reports `area` above `area_max` WHEN evaluated THEN `leaf_w` is derived from the clamped value, never negative, and the diagnostic `leaf_area_out_of_range` is raised.
- **AC-63** (auto) [LY-7, LY-15] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: rewritten as per-state active membership of the reserved slots; the earlier "two jambs" matched no `idx` scheme.)* GIVEN `fixture_socket_w2` and `fixture_socket_w3` (each with its mate) WHEN `rects_in` and `solid_in` are read in each socket state THEN the **active** slots are exactly: `FREE` — PLATE (SOLID + OCCLUDES + HULL, the whole span: `[672, 696) × [240, 336)` for W 2, `[672, 696) × [240, 384)` for W 3); `WELDED` two-sided — W 2: LEAF only (`[672, 696) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)`, absent at `leaf_w` 0); W 3: JAMB `[672, 696) × [336, 384)` plus LEAF; `WELDED` one-sided (`fixture_socket_one_sided`) — PLATE only, no LEAF and no JAMB; `CAPPED` — PLATE; `CUT_OPEN` — PLATE (SOLID + OCCLUDES + HULL, so no avatar can leave the hull and no light passes); the inactive slots are omitted from both queries; AND a low-aligned hatch means no low JAMB exists in any state; AND (lint) a world containing a `CUT_OPEN` hatch raises zero `CONTAINMENT_LEAK`.
- **AC-144** (auto) [LY-12 a, LY-15, D.9] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the stable-key invariant)* GIVEN `fixture_socket_w3` welded to its mate and then cut, once SEALED and once RAGGED WHEN the set of **reserved** `(section_id, idx)` keys is read before the weld, after the weld and after the cut THEN it is identical in all three states (static `idx` 0 and 1, LEAF 2, PLATE 3, JAMB 4 of each section); only the **active subset** changes — before: static 0, 1 and PLATE 3; welded: static 0, 1, JAMB 4 and LEAF 2 (while `leaf_w` > 0); after the cut: static 0, 1 and PLATE 3 — and no `idx` is added, removed or renumbered; a `StubEmitterVersionCache` sees the host section's `version` change at the weld and at the cut.
- **AC-169** (auto, integration) [LY-15 g, LY-16, LY-10] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: BLOCKING, the weld-time LEAF initial state)* GIVEN the `fixture_airlock` weld to `fixture_derelict_b_socket` applied in P2 of tick t (Graph `weld_join` then LM2) and `layout.doors` NOT yet run WHEN `rects_in` and `solid_in` are read over the hatch span `[672, 720) × [240, 336)` between the P2 apply and the P3 hook (a stub P2 reader) THEN both leaves are present and closed (`leaf_w` 96, rects `[672, 696) × [240, 336)` and `[696, 720) × [240, 336)`), the span is solid, no cell of the span is returned as passable, and `stale_leaf` is not raised; AND after `layout.doors` runs in P3 of tick t with `area` still 0 THEN `leaf_version` is not bumped (the cache was seeded) and the rects are unchanged; AND when the P3 `area` read is 32 (a same-tick open) THEN the leaf shrinks and `leaf_version` bumps exactly once.
- **AC-145** (auto) [LY-15 d, D.9] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN `fixture_socket_w2` (W = 2) WHEN compiled and read in every socket state THEN the JAMB slot has `idx` 2, computes to length `2 × 48 − 96 = 0`, and is **omitted in every state** (zero jambs); the before-span and after-span pieces of its run are also zero-length and omitted, so the run contributes no static rect.
- **AC-146** (auto) [LY-15 d, D.9] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN `fixture_socket_w3` (W = 3) WHEN welded two-sided THEN exactly **one** 48-px JAMB `[672, 696) × [336, 384)` is active (length `3 × 48 − 96 = 48`), beside the LEAF at `[672, 696) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)`; in `FREE`, `CAPPED` and `CUT_OPEN` the JAMB is omitted and the PLATE covers all 144 px.
- **AC-64** (auto) [LY-14, LY-15] GIVEN two mating sockets of which exactly one declares a hatch WHEN `socket_plan` runs THEN `openings[]` is empty, `pairs[]` is non-empty, the diagnostic `hatch_one_sided` is raised, no reason code is returned, and after the weld the hatched side still returns its HULL plate rect and no leaf; AND *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* the `can_attach` **preview payload** read before the weld already carries `hatch_one_sided: true` and `openings_count` 0 (and `false` / 1 for `fixture_socket_w2` with its hatched mate), with no state change and no dirty key from the preview.
- **AC-65** (auto, integration) [LY-11, LY-22] GIVEN `floor_tile_at` called on every cell of every door cell and doorway of `fixture_cryo_excerpt` WHEN evaluated THEN it returns `NONE`, and a tile for the adjacent floor; AND `loose_slots` returns the authored slots in `slot_id` ascending order; AND (lint) an authored loose item on a door cell raises `LOOSE_ON_DOOR`.
- **AC-66** (review) [LY-10, Cross-References B, Open Questions] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: inverted. The earlier text required the stale ASK to remain, so a refresh would have failed it by construction.)* GIVEN the Open Questions WHEN read THEN OQ-3 and OQ-4 are recorded as **closed**, citing the Graph's published `opening(edge_id)`, M1's `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`, `weld_join`'s `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}` and `seam_view`; the scoping of the "P2 only" correctness condition to non-virtual openings is still stated in LY-10; the `stale_leaf` diagnostic and its restore path (LY-26 c) are still specified as live behaviour; OQ-14 (c) (the door travel owner, post-MVP) is still open; AND the stale-token scan (AC-133, whose token list now includes the two stale ASK phrases and exempts this criterion's own sentence) returns zero matches over this file.

### E. Sockets, welds and the plan

- **AC-67** (auto) [D.6, LY-14] GIVEN `fixture_airlock` (E, `line_px` 696, `start_px` 240, `width_tiles` 2) and `fixture_derelict_b_socket` (W, `pos_b` (120, 144)) at `offset_a` (0, 0) WHEN `can_attach` and `socket_plan` run THEN `offset_b = (576, 96)`, B's W wall lands at `[696, 720)` abutting A's `[672, 696)`, `L_seam = 2`, `pairs[]` holds two pairs (COOLANT lane 0 and POWER lane 0) ordered by `(loop, lane_index)`, `openings[]` holds one `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)` and `reason` is empty.
- **AC-68** (auto) [D.6, LY-13] GIVEN `fixture_ns_pair` WHEN `can_attach` runs THEN `pos_a = (144, 480)`, `pos_b = (72, 96)`, `offset_b = (72, 384)` and B's N wall `[96, 120)` lands at body `y` `[480, 504)` abutting A's S wall `[456, 480)`.
- **AC-69** (auto) [D.6] GIVEN `fixture_derelict_b_bumper` (local `[96, 120) × [144, 192)`) WHEN mated THEN `GEOM_OVERLAP` and `pairs[]`, `openings[]` are empty; GIVEN `start_px` 150 THEN the template fails `GRID_24` at load, not at mate time.
- **AC-70** (auto) [LY-14] GIVEN eight single-fault inputs (a nonexistent key; a `WELDED` socket; two sockets of one body; E + E; widths 2 and 3; unequal `class_id`; unequal lane multisets; the bumper) WHEN `can_attach` runs THEN each returns exactly `SOCKET_UNKNOWN`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `SAME_BODY`, `FACING_MISMATCH`, `WIDTH_MISMATCH`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `LANE_MISMATCH`, `GEOM_OVERLAP` respectively; AND GIVEN simultaneous faults THEN the verdict is the first in that order; a `WELDED`, `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` socket answers `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` before any geometry work.
- **AC-71** (auto) [D.6, LY-3 d] GIVEN 1,000 24-grid sockets and offsets generated from the committed `SEED_AC71` (corpus asserted by count first, Story-type mapping convention) WHEN `offset_b` is computed THEN it lies on the 24 grid every time, no `OFFSET_OFF_GRID` is produced, and a mate request carrying `rot_q` or a mirror cannot be expressed (no such argument exists).
- **AC-72** (auto) [LY-14] GIVEN two welded hulls that touch away from the mated socket WHEN `can_attach` runs THEN it returns no reason, `GEOM_OVERLAP` stays silent and the diagnostic `HULL_CONTACT_OUTSIDE_SOCKET` count is 1.
- **AC-73** (auto) [LY-16] GIVEN `attach_section` after the Graph's `weld_join` WHEN applied THEN the `welds[]` row is `ACTIVE` with `welded_at_T`, both sockets are `WELDED(seam_id)`, the absorbed body is `DISSOLVED`, its sections are re-based by D.6 onto the surviving body (the body with the lower `body_id`, here body 1 of the home-ship), `version` and `static_version` are bumped for **every section whose socket state changed — the unmoved host section 1 and the moved section 3 —** and every moved section, the dirty keys are exactly `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/1`, `BODY/3`, `SEC/1` and `SEC/3` (5 keys; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the unmoved host's `SEC/1` was missing*), and the return is `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}` with `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)` for the `fixture_airlock` weld of AC-67 (**fixture value, not roster**; the authored MVP roster pair gives (696, 384), registry `mvp_template_roster`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
- **AC-150** (auto) [LY-16, D.6] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: reversed arguments)* GIVEN the `fixture_airlock` weld issued once as `attach_section(sock_airlock_e, sock_b_w, …)` and once, in a fresh world, as `attach_section(sock_b_w, sock_airlock_e, …)` WHEN both are applied THEN both produce the same surviving body (the home-ship's body 1, the lower `body_id`), the same absorbed body (3, `DISSOLVED`), `offset_b = (576, 96)`, `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)`, the same dirty keys and a **byte-identical** `welds[]` row and `layout_hash` (the row records the survivor side as `section_a`, LY-16); AND a cut of that seam then gives the new body `origin_section_id = m = 3` (D.12).
- **AC-160** (auto, lint) [LY-14, D.2, D.6] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN the static-footprint `GEOM_OVERLAP` WHEN (a) a LOW prop (SOLID, not occluding) of body B lands on a wall of body A THEN `GEOM_OVERLAP` (it would have escaped a test over `rects_in`); (b) the same mate is evaluated with a door leaf open and again closed THEN the verdict is identical (it never reads leaf state); (c) a room tile of B lands on a room tile of A (floor on floor) THEN `GEOM_OVERLAP`; (d) the two PLATE footprints of a mated pair abut at the seam line THEN no overlap; (e) the verdict is memoised on `(socket_a, socket_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)` and a door animating on either body does not invalidate the memo.
- **AC-161** (auto) [LY-14, UI Requirements] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN `can_attach` called as a pure preview for (a) `fixture_socket_w2` with its hatched mate, (b) `fixture_socket_w2` with a hatchless mate, (c) a failing pair (`FACING_MISMATCH`) THEN the payload is (a) `{reason: none, hatch_one_sided: false, openings_count: 1}`, (b) `{none, true, 0}`, (c) `{FACING_MISMATCH, false, 0}`, and no call changes state, marks a dirty key or consumes an id.
- **AC-74** (auto) [LY-27, CR-9] GIVEN LM1-LM4 WHEN each is invoked with a failing `can_*` THEN no state changes, no dirty key is marked and no id is consumed; GIVEN a passing `can_*` alone (validate without apply) THEN nothing changes either; GIVEN the Graph M1 stub configured to fail inside `build_section`'s apply THEN the kernel enters `FAULTED` and the failure is logged.
- **AC-75** (auto) [LY-27] GIVEN the public API WHEN scanned THEN no `install_cap_plate` or `set_socket_state` mutator exists and a socket's state changes only inside LM2 and LM3.
- **AC-76** (lint) [LY-13, LY-14, LY-30] GIVEN one fixture per case WHEN linted THEN a hatch socket with `width_tiles` 1 raises `HATCH_WIDTH`; a hatch whose `doorway_start_px` differs from its socket's `start_px` raises `HATCH_ALIGN`; a socket in an interior wall `SOCKET_ON_EXTERIOR`; two sockets 1 tile apart `SOCKET_SPACING` (2 passes, `SOCKET_SPACING_MIN_TILES` 2); an occupied outward half-tile `SOCKET_APPROACH_FREE`; 5 sockets `SOCKET_COUNT` (4 passes, `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` 4); a lane with no Graph-template node `LANE_UNRESOLVED`; a 3-tile socket with one hatch and a 1-tile socket with no hatch pass. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-77** (auto) [LY-13] GIVEN the loaded MVP world WHEN evaluated THEN it holds exactly one home-ship socket and its mate on derelict B (LSG:228), and every section has at most `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` (4) sockets, itself at most `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION` (8).
- **AC-78** (review) [LY-13] GIVEN the Open Questions WHEN read THEN the socket economy (a weld-then-cut leaves the one MVP home-ship socket terminal) is stated with the three options (a re-cut verb keeping history, more home-ship sockets, derelicts bring at least 3 sockets), the net-cycle arithmetic and the reopen condition "a second weld enters scope".

### F. Cuts, detach, bodies and discard

- **AC-79** (auto) [D.12, LY-17] GIVEN `fixture_chain` (built and welded as pinned in the fixture table: `next_body_id` is 5 before the cut) WHEN seam (1, 3) is cut THEN components are `{1}` and `{3, 4}`, body 1 keeps `{1}`, `{3, 4}` gets body id **5** (the previous `next_body_id`; it becomes 6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: expected integers pinned)*, `frame_shift = (576, 96)`, new offsets are (0, 0) and (480, 0), sockets become `CAPPED` (SEALED) or `CUT_OPEN` (RAGGED), the weld row is `CUT_SEALED` / `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`, the new body's `origin_section_id` is 3, and the dirty keys are exactly **six**: `S/<seam>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>`, `SEC/1`, `SEC/3`, `SEC/4` (`SEC/1` because section 1's socket state changed although it did not move; the earlier count of four omitted the kept body and section 1); `version` and `static_version` are bumped for sections 1, 3 and 4. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-182** (auto) [LY-12 d, LY-16, LY-17] *(Added 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, Emitter body_id/weld GAP)* GIVEN `fixture_chain` and a weld or a cut WHEN `changed_region` is read in the same tick THEN the two socket-host sections report REGION whose box equals the union of that socket's PLATE, JAMB and LEAF slot rectangles (active and inactive) in the section's body frame, every other moved section reports FRAME (a pure translation, `rot_q` 0, slot sets unchanged), and a read in the next tick reports NONE for them; AND build, discard and `post_restore` report ALL, a `layout.doors` leaf change reports REGION(union of the old and new leaf rectangles), and after a restore every section reports ALL once; AND the cut's LM3 record carries `rects[]` equal to `detach_preview(seam_id).rects[]`.
- **AC-149** (auto) [LY-17, LY-12 d] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the see-through-but-solid failure)* GIVEN the `fixture_airlock` weld with the hatch open at `area` 32 (the kept section's leaf `[672, 696) × [240, 288)`, so a gap `[288, 336)` passes light) and a `StubEmitterVersionCache` that has cached the kept section's occluders WHEN the seam is cut (once SEALED, once RAGGED) THEN the kept section's `version` **and** `static_version` have changed, its dirty key `SEC/1` was marked, a `StubEmitterVersionCache` read in the same tick rebuilds, and `rects_in` and `solid_in` now return the PLATE `[672, 696) × [240, 336)` (SOLID + OCCLUDES + HULL) and no leaf; a segment test through the former gap `[288, 336)` is blocked; the same holds for the moved section 3.
- **AC-174** (auto, integration, `StubBodyFootBoxes` + `StubAssembly`) [LY-17, LY-18, MSA-21] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the entombment guard)* GIVEN the `fixture_airlock` weld with the hatch open at `area` 32 and a foot-box stub `[680, 696) × [296, 304)` standing in the open hatch passage (it overlaps the PLATE footprint `[672, 696) × [240, 336)` that a cut would materialise) WHEN (a) the CHANNEL path completes a cut THEN the Assembly stub's completion `validate` returns `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED` and `detach_section` is never reached; (b) the crisis path calls `detach_section` directly THEN Layout applies it and places the PLATE **without reading the stub** (a recording stub confirms Layout made zero calls to `foot_boxes`), `solid_in` over the box returns the PLATE, and the Body stub returns `-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP` from BM4 given `record.rects`, asserted in Body AC-BDY-140/141; this test pins that Layout reads no actor state, that the record carries `rects[]` equal to the preview's, and that the overlap is observable as `overlap == true` (AC-28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
- **AC-80** (auto) [D.12, LY-17] GIVEN `fixture_chain_origin4` (the chain of the fixture table restored from the committed snapshot with body 1's `origin_section_id` = 4, offsets unchanged, `next_body_id` 5) WHEN seam (1, 3) is cut THEN `C_keep` = `{3, 4}` (it contains the origin 4) keeps body id **1** with offsets (576, 96) and (1056, 96) unchanged, the NEW id **5** goes to `{1}` (`next_body_id` becomes 6), `m = 1`, `frame_shift = offset_old(1) = (0, 0)`, the new body's `origin_section_id` is 1 and section 1's new offset is (0, 0) (re-based to the minimum section id of the new component) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: build order, body ids and frame shift pinned)*.
- **AC-81** (auto) [LY-14, LY-17] GIVEN the sequences of legal welds and cuts over five sections generated from the committed `SEED_AC81` (corpus asserted by count first, Story-type mapping convention; *amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: seeds kept, not dropped*) WHEN every cut is applied THEN exactly two components result each time, and a ring cannot be built (`SAME_BODY`).
- **AC-82** (review) [LY-17] GIVEN the public API of `detach_section` and every read WHEN scanned THEN `detach_section` takes only `(seam_id, boundary_mode)` and no mutator or read accepts a cut position or compartment id.
